findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review hand washing with staff and conduct oversight as needed. Ensure proper hand washing at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the inspector observed the bar three part sink to have a low concentration in their sanitizing bin. The PIC was notified and strengthened the newly made solution to correctly. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to use a sanitizer rag to wipe down a counter, and then immediately put on gloves and begin handling foods. No hand washing was observed. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing practices with staff and ensure that hand washing is taking place at all times that it should be.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). 

The ice scoop in the bar area is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This situation would require the bartender’s hand to come into contact with the Ready-To-Eat (RTE) food (ice) when grabbing the scoop. Education was conducted and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that bare hands are not put into contact with RTE foods at any time.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

On arrival the kitchen hand sink was blocked by cases of soda syrup and a step ladder. The items were moved during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen area was without paper towels. The PIC was notified and paper towels supplied during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wiping cloths in the kitchen were observed sitting outside of the sanitizer bucket.  Sanitizing cloths used to wipe food contact surfaces must be held in the sanitizer solution between uses.  Ensure clothes are kept in sanitizer buckets to sanitize used cloths and also to prevent the cloths to become contaminated between uses.

3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine had a sanitizer concentration of 0 ppm (cl) at time of inspection.  The machine was ran 3-4 times and the line was primed with no change.  Discussed with PIC, sanitize dishes in 3 part sink until machine is serviced.  Check sanitizer concentration of dish machine daily to ensure it is sanitizing dishes properly.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Sausage was observed thawing out on the counter at room temperature.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure frozen foods are thawed in a cooler or submerged under running water to prevent contamination. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. 

Pasta noodles cooked at 7am, probed at 2PM at 70 degrees. Cooling did not occur in the allotted time frames (above). Discussed cooling process with PIC, although running water was used to facilitate cooling, it did not sufficiently cool. Consider adding a couple pitchers of ice to the running water and use probe thermometer to verify it is cooling properly. COS- PIC voluntarily discarded the pasta.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less.
Prep cooler on line showing ambient temperatures of 53 degrees. Salami in top of prep cooler probed at 52 degrees and burger patties in bottom of prep cooler probed at 51 degrees. Employee was unsure of prep time as there was a shift change at 2pm. Discussed with PIC cold holding temperatures and operation practices in a hot and humid kitchen. (oftentimes cold holding equipment cannot sustain temperatures in these conditions). All meats within cooler were voluntarily discarded. Sliced onions, tomatoes, and jalapenos kept because they were smaller quantities and appeared to be recently prepped (full). Thawing chicken wings, still observed partially frozen, were moved to walk-in cooler to continue cooling. 

During inspector write up of report, PIC informed that flour was blocking the air intake of the cooler and employee vacuumed it out and the thermometer was now reading 45 degrees, decreased within an hour.

findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: hot running water, liquid hand soap, and disposable paper towels. 

Upon arrival, handsink in kitchen was not equipped with liquid handsoap. Inspector informed PIC and handsoap was replaced immediately.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.16  (C) Multiple areas along Eastern wall in kitchen (facing Spring St) are in a state of disrepair/have areas vulnerable to pest access. Also, wall behind walk-in cooler and dish area has holes in bricks that may be contributing to pest presence. At this time, no evidence of mice getting access to food in dry storage or walk in cooler observed. 
Inspector observed mice droppings along these areas and 2-5 traps located along these walls. PIC reported Adams is PCO and they treat facility monthly. Discussed pest control efforts, items that can be addressed to mitigate problems. 
1)Have Adams treat facility more than once a month until presence is mitigated. Possibly switch up chemicals/traps methods used per their discretion. 
2)Conduct a walk through on inside/outside of building with PCO. Note areas that provide potential access to mice and seal/spackle/treat accordingly. 
3) Establish routine cleaning schedule where larger equipment (dough mixer, fridges, dolly) is moved aside and hard-to-reach corners are deep cleaned. **Excess debris provides an environment for them to thrive. 
4)Place dry good items in sealed totes to prevent pest access, and to make it easy to move inventory around for cleaning.
PIC described some renovations planned in the dish/walk-in area in near future. Ensure this item is addressed when renovations occur.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer prepared during food prep.  Sanitizer buckets prepared upon request.

750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed a container of cheese sauce in the walk-in cooler with no date mark. Provide a date mark on all potentially hazardous foods. A label of 08/27 was provided on the container of cheese sauce during the inspection to correct the violation. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.comment:
CORRECTED: Observed an employee improperly washing their hands by turning the faucet off with their bare hands. Properly wash your hands. The employee properly washed their hands during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.
